resolution: Three different uses share the words 'per se': a per se ordered series (prima via, `MovesAsMoved`), being necessary per se (tertia via, `IsNecessaryPerSe`: no cause of necessity from elsewhere), and being self-evident (per se notum; in this corpus the `self_evident` marking). Each is its own predicate or record field and no inference moves between them: the convergence result TERTIA-VIA-NECESSARY-PER-SE-IS-MAXIME-ENS uses only `IsNecessaryPerSe`, and the self-evidence of STMT-EXCLUDED-MIDDLE rests on Aristotle's elenctic defence, not on per se ordering. The natural-law per-se-nota reading is Aquinas’s predicate-in-the-subject account of self-evidence. A claim proposing this account is not already a corpus self_evident marking. Not forked (sense fork batch 3, #1233 B): the senses are homonyms, not rival readings of one use. The two propositional senses already have distinct Lean declarations of different types (DEF-PER-SE-ORDERED-SERIES: NoInfinitePerSeMoverSeriesReading over a moving relation; DEF-NECESSARY-PER-SE: IsNecessaryPerSe, a predicate of beings with a cause-of-necessity relation), so substituting one for the other at any root-path use is already a type error. The two epistemic senses (DEF-SELF-EVIDENT-MARKING, a corpus record marking; DEF-NATURAL-LAW-PER-SE-NOTA, a status of propositions) are not propositions about beings and have no Lean declaration to substitute. No root-path step admits two of the four senses, so no coverage or exclusivity premise has a use to range over. The rival-relevant split inside the first sense, per se versus per accidens ordering, is DISAMB-PER-SE-LINK's (needs: a step whose one use admits two senses).
